Loss-of-function mutations in both PRKN (associated with AR-JP) and OPTN (associated with ALS12) impair the process of mitophagy. This leads to the accumulation of damaged mitochondria and dysfunctional proteins, which in turn promotes protein aggregation, ultimately resulting in neurodegeneration characteristic of Parkinsonism and motor neuron degeneration.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in PRKN and OPTN have entirely distinct downstream cellular effects unrelated to mitochondrial quality control or protein homeostasis, or that the identified causal variants for both diseases are common in the general population (e.g., >1% allele frequency in gnomAD).
